body.summary: Back-fills the ledger entry for work implemented and committed earlier without its BUILD record. All ten tasks have commits (t1 3f033aa, t2 70ed25e, t3 2465678, t4 be417da, t5 35aec0e, t6 4b3c0a7, t7 b7513ce, t8 3b3d69c, t9 2ba2838, t10 e15ef63) plus three code-review fixes (404232d CR-1/CR-2, 6c7d221 CR-3 making the rangeBase stamp write-once). Verified now, not inherited: the build-runner and build-step suites run 153 tests, 153 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped on Node 22 with INSRC_LIVE_TESTS unset, and tsc is clean. The validate gate could not execute anything in its sandbox, so I re-ran the one mutation proof it reported as unrecorded: re-introducing t8's absent-sizeClass interpolation turns 5 tests red, including both byte-identity goldens, so that coverage is genuinely non-vacuous. ACCEPTED DEVIATION, recorded rather than passed silently: t10's acceptance check requires all three of t1's characterisations to be INVERTED by their named task, and TEST C was instead re-labelled "NOT a defect" at t6. The rationale holds — that scenario is a trivial standalone with neither PLAN nor LLD, so there is no upstream artifact to carry a stamped base, and an empty change set is the specified outcome for that route rather than a bug; the genuine t6 inversion is the separate clean-tree-with-a-stamped-base test. The check as written is therefore amended to cover TEST C by re-label, and the t10 audit test already encodes that expectation. CORRECTION TO THIS STORY'S OWN t4/t9 DECISION, applied here: this record's first write landed under docs/epics/ although the work item is standalone, because the shared validate persist omitted meta.standalone so mergeWithPrior could carry a prior forward — which works on a second write but not a first, where the absent key reads as false. The persist layer's "absent means epic" default is correct and unchanged; the caller was abstaining from a route it could read. The validate writer now resolves it via inheritedStandalone, exactly as completion-record.ts already did, under the same `=== true` guard so only an explicit true is ever written and a prior true can still survive. Two new tests pin both halves and the standalone one is mutation-verified. KNOWN LIMITATION, not fixed: the change set is derived from rangeBase..HEAD where rangeBase is stamped at plan approval, so back-filling a Story days later sweeps every unrelated commit since — the first attempt here produced 169 entries naming other Stories' records. The change set below was instead derived from this Story's own twelve commits. Prompt validation is unaffected; a stale-base back-fill is the case the range answer does not cover.
